title: Dissonance
subtitle: A soul-stirring swell of noise, appreciated even by old-school rock fans.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Hey, the Nukutai nutjobs outside are gone! Don't tell me they've abandoned ship and left us here to starve!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Come back here, you yellow-bellied cowards! This pirate is not going to Davy Jones's locker without a fight!
Having satisfied her anger by yelling through the porthole, she turns to the others.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Sonetto, are those solvents working at all? Tell me they are!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: It appears the outer layer of the door has already dissolved substantially.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Excellent. The Papyrpillar Solvents are more effective than I anticipated.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: At this rate, the door should be fully dissolved in approximately 13 hours!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Oh wow, that fast! Really, Fish Tank? I'll be waiting with bated breath!
She furiously shakes his glass tank.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Hey, why don't you just whip us up a few helmets like yours?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: That way, you can just blast the door open with the TNT, and we'll be sound as a pound. Well, our heads at least.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: My helmet is made of regular silica, 7.092% calcium magnesium carbonate, and 3.27% aluminum oxide. I'm afraid it's no more explosion-proof than your regular old skull.
Regulus slumps against the door as the last vestiges of resistance leave her body.
A faint shout comes from the other side of the door.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Regulus, I'd stay away from the door if I were you.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Huh?!

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: They're here!

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: Hold onto this anchor like your life depends on it!

items.speaker: Helmsman Charlie
items.text: We ram the door open on the count of three!
The helmsmen's voices are like music to their ears.

items.speaker: Helmsmen
items.text: Three!
A countdown begins.

items.speaker: Helmsmen
items.text: Two!
A nearly soul-stirring impact.

items.speaker: Helmsmen
items.text: One!
With their final count, the supposedly unbreakable door collapses.
The cheering of familiar faces echoes through the room.
Regulus swears it's the most beautiful noise she's ever heard.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Right on! I knew you'd come through for us, Barcarola! A rising star through hell or high water!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You have our thanks, Ms. Barcarola.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I just want to save as many people as possible, for the pride of the "Free Breeze"!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We aim to do the same thing.
After a pause, Ulrich steps forward.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Timekeeper, I need to get to the radio room.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: It's likely to be the only place on the ship that we'll be able to get through their jamming.
She turns to Ulrich with a solemn look on her face.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I'll bring good news. I promise.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I see. Regulus, you should go with him.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: No, no, no, I don't need additional manpower for such an easy—

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I insist. We can't afford to lose anyone, Mr. Ulrich.
She places a compact device in his leather-gloved hand.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: This is ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The Pioneers Mk I positioning system, the latest in technology from Laplace.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: But if I recall correctly, it's never been mass-produced. Only a few prototypes were made available.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And this is one of them. If anything happens, someone can use it to track you down if you're in serious trouble, like if you've fallen into the sea.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: This will surely come in handy. Thanks, Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Good luck, Mr. Ulrich.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ha, he won't need it, because no one knows radio systems better than this captain!
She nods before the two vanish around the corner.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The rest of us need to return to the lobby and get the masked guests under control.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, do we have sufficient sedatogens left?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Yes, Timekeeper. We still have plenty!
She turns to the helmsmen.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Gentlemen, I'll need your assistance, too.

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: Of course, ma'am. Ms. Barcarola already told us everything. Sounds like helping you means we're helping ourselves!

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Esam, do you know where we can find the spare keys to the passenger cabins?

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: We have another friend to free.
Elsewhere on the ship, two stealthy figures navigate through the darkness.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Are you sure this is the right way?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Are you doubting my capabilities?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Not exactly.
Broadcast Room
The broadcasting room is empty.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: It's only that I expected they'd have this place locked down like the crown jewels, but nobody is here.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: We'll concern ourselves with that later.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Let's get to work, Regulus!
Ignoring Regulus's wandering about, Ulrich quickly channels his "thought current" into the broadcasting console.

items.speaker: "VHF Radio"
items.text: Coastal base station, come in! Coastal base station, come in!

items.speaker: "VHF Radio"
items.text: Where's the International Maritime Organization when you need them?!

items.speaker: "VHF Radio"
items.text: Laplace Australia branch, please come in! Laplace Australia branch, please come in!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I just checked out the wiring. All the signal transmitters have been sabotaged.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: No wonder there's been no sight nor sound of those oily freaks!
Ulrich seems unsurprised. Retracting his "thought current," he disregards the apparent predicament.
He lays one peculiar item after another onto the table.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Reel it in, Fish Tank. You're not conducting the "Artificial Storm" experiments right here, are you?!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Why not? We have a supernatural phenomenon, a vast water supply, sufficient asymmetrical nuclide R, and the required sound wave frequency ready in the transmission system here.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: If these aren't the perfect testing conditions for the "Artificial Storm," then what is?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Wha-wait, wait, wait!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Are you forgetting what you just said to Vertin? What about all those side effects? You've got no bleeding idea how severe they'll be, or how long they'll last!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Which is why it's lucky you were sent along with me, Regulus. If anything happens to me, you'll have to be the one to report the experiments' results!
He gives her a hearty pat on the shoulder.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Whether the "Storm" comes or not, we'll have made an undeniable leap of progress.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: More than worth a bit of Storm Syndrome, no matter how nasty.
He tosses an Equilibrium Umbrella into Regulus's hands.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: At least now you'll have an extra Equilibrium Umbrella.
He pays no mind to his immobile teammate.
Instead, he meticulously sorts through the materials he has spread on the table.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ulrich!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I refuse to be a part of this!
